newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-POLL INTERRUPTS AUSTRALIAN, U.S. DOMINATION.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POLL INTERRUPTS AUSTRALIAN, U.S. DOMINATION.

text.p: World number one and Olympic champion Claudia Poll swam the third fastest time ever to win the 200 metres freestyle on the opening day of the Pan Pacific championships on Sunday.

On a day dominated by Australia and the U.S., who won three gold medals apiece, Costa Rican Poll pulled steadily away from Chinese Le Jingyi and finished in one minute 57.48 seconds. Le clocked 2:00:54.
Australia's Susie O'Neill outclassed the joint U.S. challenge of Misty Hyman and Kristine Quance to win the women's 200 butterfly in 2.08:59, the best time for the event this year.
The expected challenge from Hyman never materialised as, after leading over the first 50 metres, she faded and was then caught by Quance on the last length for second place.
Other Australian winners were Michael Klim, who swam a 1997 best 1.47:60 in the men's 200 freestyle, and Grant Hackett in the men's 800 freestyle.
Hackett was in a class of his own with a time of 7.50:30, making him the third fastest in the event.
Only compatriots Kieren Perkins and Daniel Kowalski have been faster than 17-year-old Hackett.
Russia-born Lenny Krayzelburg won the men's 100 backstroke in 54:43 -- the fastest this year -- and makes him the second-fastest American in the event behind Jeff Rouse.
"It was a pretty good race and is a good stepping stone for the worlds," he said. The world championships are in January in Perth.
Ugur Taner also become the second-fastest American, after Melvin Stewart, in the 200 butterfly with a winning time of 1.57:35.
The other American to win was Brooke Bennett in the women's 1,500 freestyle in 16.10:24.
